solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tense as tempting confections wheeled over

indicators.note: something wheeled over is turned end to end, so the word for the confections is read backwards

parts.note: desserts are sweet dishes that tempt diners

explanation.surface: A diner grows anxious as a trolley of tempting puddings is wheeled across the restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheeled over' turns DESSERTS round; the famous observation that one word is the other backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tense is under strain, anxious and wound up: the adjective is a synonym.

clue.text: Grate pickle

definitions.meaning: to grate is to ... against a surface
a pickle is a predicament, a tricky situation

explanation.surface: Grating a pickled vegetable in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrape means both to rub abrasively and an awkward fix one gets into.

clue.text: A current novel inspiring old storyteller

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the rearranged letters take in the letter for old
novel means new, so the letters of these words take a new order

explanation.surface: A current novel inspires an old-fashioned storyteller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' turns A CURRENT into RACNTEUR, which takes in O after RAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A raconteur is someone who tells anecdotes skilfully, a storyteller.

clue.text: Capital opposed to a deity, eastern church feeds spreading of lies

indicators.note: the pieces feed into the scrambled letters, going inside them
spreading the letters of the word scatters them into a new order

parts.note: anti means against, opposed to
a god is a deity

explanation.surface: An atheist capital where an eastern church spreads lies about God.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading of' scrambles LIES to SILE; ANTI-A-GOD-E-CH goes in after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the full name of Chile's capital city, usually called just Santiago.

clue.text: Point about that is: last of clues the first to be solved, perhaps?

definitions.text: the first to be solved, perhaps?

indicators.note: the compass point goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: east is a point of the compass
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A solver notes that the final clue was, in fact, the first one cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: EAST goes about IE and S (last of 'clues'). The definition is speculative, hence 'perhaps?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The simplest clue is likely the one cracked first, so the most straightforward is a fair description.

clue.text: Goal that's material

definitions.meaning: an aim or purpose, as in 'the ... of the exercise'
something material is a physical thing, a thing you can touch

explanation.surface: A goal that is tangible rather than abstract.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an aim one pursues and a physical thing, the material item itself.

clue.text: Punk rock star brand I'm building

indicators.note: punk suggests something rough and wild, so the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A punk rock star announces he is building his own brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punk' reads as music but is the anagram signal for ROCK STAR BRAND I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: Bricks and mortar is an idiom for buildings and property, physical construction.

clue.text: Two times oxygen required for inspiration

parts.note: two words for time: an era and T, the abbreviation for time
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Twice the oxygen is needed to breathe in deeply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiration' is not breathing in but a Muse, the source of a poet's inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry, a source of poetic inspiration.

clue.text: Little sticks for pond life

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
poles are long sticks

explanation.surface: Using little sticks to poke at the creatures in a pond.
explanation.definitionFit: Tadpoles are frog larvae living in ponds, so they are an example of pond life.

clue.text: Space rocket initially travelling an astronomically long way?

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move about, so they take a new order
initially means take the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A space rocket covers an enormous distance on its voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling' shuffles SPACE plus R, the initial of 'rocket'.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsec is a unit of distance in astronomy, about 3.26 light years, hence a long way.

clue.text: Poisonous stuff in turmeric, I noted

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words 'turmeric, I noted', spanning the comma

explanation.surface: A cook spots something toxic lurking in the turmeric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters inside 'tuRMERIC, I Noted': RIC from turmeric, I, and N from noted.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricin is a deadly toxin extracted from castor beans, so it is poisonous stuff.

clue.text: Enclosed by desert, western country snubbing British nation

indicators.note: being enclosed by the desert word means the other letters go inside it

parts.note: a sandy desert: sand

indicators.note: snubbing means ignoring, so the British letters are left out of the country

parts.note: Brazil is a South American country

explanation.surface: A western country, landlocked by desert, cold-shoulders Britain in a diplomatic row.
explanation.walkthrough: The western country is not the nation defined: it is the South American one, losing its British letters, which sits after W inside the desert word.
explanation.definitionFit: Swaziland, now officially Eswatini, is an independent southern African kingdom, so a nation.

clue.text: Unable to write about end of destitution, one broke

indicators.note: the phrase for lacking a writing tool goes about, around, the other letters

parts.note: with no pen you cannot write: penless

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A broke writer, too poor to buy a pen, cannot write about destitution.
explanation.walkthrough: N (end of 'destitution') and I go inside PENLESS: PEN-NI-LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being broke means having no money at all, which is exactly what penniless means.

clue.text: Eastern city right about fiddle backfiring

indicators.note: backfiring sends the whole construction backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
the word for right goes around the word for fiddle

parts.note: OK means all right, correct
to toy with something is to fiddle with it

explanation.surface: A scam in an Eastern city goes wrong, the fiddle backfiring on its perpetrator.
explanation.walkthrough: OK about TOY gives OTOYK; 'backfiring' reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Kyoto is a historic city in Japan, the Far East, its former imperial capital.

clue.text: By one's ear, hang on heavy load

indicators.note: judged by the ear, the word is identified by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to hang on is to wait

explanation.surface: A worker hangs on, ear straining, under a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: WAIT and WEIGHT are pronounced alike; 'By one's ear' signals the sound match.
explanation.definitionFit: A weight is something heavy to carry, a burden or heavy load.

clue.text: Arguably dirtier exhibitionist starts after cleaner act

indicators.note: the starts come after the cleaner's word in the answer

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a British word for a cleaner

indicators.note: the starts of the three words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A rather grubby exhibitionist begins performing once the cleaner has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: CHAR (British for a cleaning woman) is followed by ADE, the starts of 'Arguably dirtier exhibitionist'.
explanation.definitionFit: A charade is a pretence, an absurd show put on to deceive: an act.

clue.text: Collected by cab, and one duly left

indicators.note: the letters are collected by, held within, the run of words 'cab, and one duly'

explanation.surface: Picked up by a cab, everyone duly left.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through 'cAB AND ONE Duly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left behind and deserted has been forsaken, a synonym in the past participle.

clue.text: Lip on short piece of glass vessel

parts.note: lip is cheek, impudence, which is also sauce

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: a pane is a sheet of glass in a window

explanation.surface: A lip resting on a broken piece of glass from a drinking vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lip' looks like the rim of the vessel but means cheek, SAUCE; 'short' docks PANE to PAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucepan is a cooking pot, one kind of kitchen vessel.

clue.text: A part of the nose, cut

parts.note: the bridge is the bony ridge at the top of the nose

explanation.surface: A piece of the nose has been cut, as after a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, to cut it down.

clue.text: Require English with translation of Latin

indicators.note: a translation renders the word into different form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A course that requires English along with translation from Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation of' rearranges LATIN to NTAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to involve as a necessary consequence, so to require.

clue.text: Once more depict turning of screw

indicators.note: turning the word round means reading the prison officer's title backwards

parts.note: screw is British slang for a prison warder

explanation.surface: An engineer draws the turning of a screw a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screw' is not the hardware but British prison slang for a warder; 'turning of' reverses WARDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraw something is to draw or depict it again, making a fresh picture.

clue.text: Free from responsibility, again experience overwhelming pleasure, finally

indicators.note: overwhelming means covering over, so the letters for reliving go around the other letter

parts.note: to relive something is to experience it again

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Release from duty lets one experience overwhelming pleasure once more.
explanation.walkthrough: E, the last of 'pleasure', goes inside RELIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone of a duty is to free them from it, taking it off their hands.

clue.text: A shade hot, stripped off over mountains

indicators.note: stripping the outer layer leaves only the middle letter of the word

parts.note: a range is a chain of mountains

explanation.surface: A hot sunbather strips off over the mountains and acquires a tan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot, stripped off' leaves O; 'over' puts it above RANGE in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange is a colour, and a colour is a shade.

clue.text: Metropolitan running both ways?

definitions.note: the word meaning to do with a city is itself all the wordplay, its letters the same in either direction

indicators.note: a word that runs both ways reads identically forwards and backwards

parts.note: the word meaning to do with a city is itself all the wordplay, its letters the same in either direction

explanation.surface: A city route that runs in both directions.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a palindrome; 'running' also hints at a city's traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Civic means relating to a city or town, as does metropolitan.

clue.text: Express love in wicked behaviour

indicators.note: the letter for love goes in the word for wicked behaviour

parts.note: vice is immoral or wicked behaviour
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Declaring one's love in the middle of wicked behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice an opinion is to express it, putting it into words.

clue.text: Coffee requested in twelve- ounce cup? That's unlikely to happen

definitions.text: Coffee requested in twelve- ounce cup?
definitions.meaning: in coffee chains a tall is the twelve-ounce size, so asking for one is placing that kind of order
a demand so difficult it is hardly going to be met

explanation.surface: A barista hears a customer's coffee request and doubts it will be fulfilled.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a very demanding request, one unlikely to be met, and literally a request for a tall coffee.

clue.text: Proper computer lessons I have, simple

parts.note: prim means proper, correct in a stiff way
IT, information technology, is the school subject about computers
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A student boasts of proper computer lessons that are simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive means basic, crude or unsophisticated, so a near synonym of simple.

clue.text: Figure running joint

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A figure of a running joint, perhaps a knee on a jogger.
explanation.definitionFit: In carpentry a tenon is the projecting tongue of a mortise-and-tenon joint.

clue.text: Nice gutless journalists required

indicators.note: with its guts removed only the outer letters of the word remain

parts.note: two editors, ED twice, make the plural journalists

explanation.surface: Cowardly journalists in Nice were needed for a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, but here it only supplies its outer letters NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Needed and required are synonyms in the past participle: wanted, necessary.

clue.text: Envy what vagrant might do with Dickensian simpleton

parts.note: a homeless vagrant might beg for money
Barnaby Rudge is the simple-minded hero of the Dickens novel of that name

explanation.surface: Someone envies a beggar's carefree life alongside a Dickens character.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge someone something is to resent their having it, which is to envy them.
